issues:
The checker's evidence has three errors, and it missed two papers.
(1) Missed: Kunin et al., NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv 2506.06489), App. F.2.2, Thm F.7, Eq. (85). Minimising the MSE cost over aligned quadratic neurons at one frequency reaches equality iff sum_i A_w A_u A_v e^{i(s_w +/- (s_u - s_v))} = 0 and sum_i A_w A_u A_v e^{i(s_w + s_u + s_v)} = 0 (along with square-term conditions); Eq. 92 then leaves only cos(... + 2pi xi (c-a-b)/p). This is the finite system (JF) at n=2 with arbitrary amplitudes, so 'JF not found' is false for n=2.
(2) Missed at this item: Tian, NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv 2410.01779), Lemma 1. Its 0-set R_c = {r_{k1k2k}: not all equal} contains exactly the same-frequency sign-flipped copies (Table 1 columns a-bar b c, a b-bar c, a b c-bar) plus cross-frequency terms, so it is strictly stronger than def:if. The order-3 solution rho(u_syn) = u^2+u+1 is three equal-weight nodes with DFT chain vectors, i.e. the n=2 nu-block. Fig. 2 (bottom): with the R* term dropped, GD finds 'exactly 3 hidden nodes' per frequency. The loss is MSE and there is no lower bound. The repo sweep already lists Tian for the nu-block, but not at def:if.
(3) He et al. (2602.16849) is described backwards. In App. B.1 (Eq. B.1), Def. 4.1(iii) removes cos(w(x-y-/+j)) (iota=2) and cos(w(x+y+j)) (iota=4), i.e. every non-empty T. The surviving 2x/2y peaks sit at modes (2k,0;-k) and (0,2k;-k), which is other-mode interference that def:if explicitly allows. I checked this numerically at p=13: N=3 phases {0, pi/3, 2pi/3} give beta_T = 0 for every non-empty T, while one neuron gives |beta_T| = |beta|. So He's full diversification IS def:if (equal-magnitude case), and its minimal realisation is the nu-block. It is not a mere cousin.
(4) The Zhong et al. Clock/Pizza claim is false. The idealised Pizza logit |cos(w(a-b)/2)|cos(w(a+b-c)) has beta_{j,T} = 0 for every non-empty T and every j (checked numerically at p=13), because its a-b modulation sits at modes (k+m, k-m; -k) with m != 0. It must not be cited as what def:if excludes; at most it illustrates the allowed other-mode interference.
(5) Confirmed: Morwani App. F.2 (8 neurons per frequency, 'same value on all incorrect labels c', satisfying C.1') and App. G ('every term other than Pi x_Si cancels out'); Li App. E.2 (2^{2k-1} neurons per frequency, Condition 3.8); Gromov Eqs. 11-15 ('destructive interference condition', random phases); Doshi (ICLR 2024 BGPT workshop, 'vanish due to random phase approximation').
Process note for the orchestrator: this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) when this task started, so every later verifier gets no search results. I verified by pulling arXiv PDFs with curl instead.
corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN, with the definition itself KNOWN for n=2. Exact cancellation of the same-frequency sign-flipped copies across neurons is stated as an explicit condition in Kunin et al. 2025 (Thm F.7, MSE optimality), Tian 2025 (R_c, zero-loss conditions, with a 3-node nu-block) and He et al. 2026 (Def. 4.1(iii), equal magnitudes). Exact all-n constructions are in Morwani App. F.2 and Li App. E. New: the general-n logit-table class separated from other-mode interference, its use as the margin-maximisation class, the general-n sign rule, and the nu^{1-r} cost lemma with its equality case. Revise the text to credit Kunin/Tian/He for n=2, and drop Zhong as an example of excluded interference.

extra_citations.why: Thm F.7 / Eq. (85) (App. F.2.2): the equality case of the MSE cost bound over aligned quadratic neurons requires the amplitude-weighted phase sums of the sign-flipped copies (s_w +/- (s_u - s_v), s_w + s_u + s_v) to vanish, which is exactly (JF) at n=2 with general amplitudes. Eq. 92: only cos(...(c-a-b)) survives. Cite at def:if as prior n=2 form of the condition.

Lemma 1: the 0-set R_c (r_{k1k2k}=0 unless all indices are equal) contains the sign-flipped copies and is stronger than def:if. Table 1 / Fig. 2: rho(u_syn) = u^2+u+1 is a 3-node per-frequency solution with cube-root-of-unity phases, the n=2 nu-block, and GD finds exactly 3 nodes per frequency when the R* term is dropped. The loss is MSE, with no lower bound.
